programs.nl_rule:
The input grid has a uniform background color filling most cells. Embedded in the grid are one or more small cross-shaped or T-shaped figures composed of a secondary color. Each figure contains exactly one cell of a unique 'special' color (different from both the background and the figure's main color). The special color cell is positioned at one edge of its figure — top, bottom, left, or right — indicating a direction pointing outward from the figure toward the nearest grid border.

For each figure: (1) Identify the special color cell and determine which edge of the figure it occupies — this gives the direction the special color 'fires' toward the nearest border. (2) Starting from the special color cell, place a dot of that special color every 2 cells along the firing direction (skipping one cell, coloring the next, repeating) until reaching the grid border. (3) Fill the entire border wall that the ray hits with the special color (the full row if firing up/down, or the full column if firing left/right). (4) Where two colored border walls meet at a corner cell, set that corner cell to black (.). All other cells remain unchanged.

The output grid has the same dimensions as the input. The background and all embedded figures remain in place. The only additions are: colored border walls along edges where rays terminate, ray dots every 2 cells between figures and their target borders, and black corner cells where two colored borders intersect.
